📌 Tehran, IRNA — Following the aggressive act committed by the US on Wednesday evening, targeting a point close to a children’s cancer hospital in Iran’s Ahvaz, the foreign ministry spokesperson described the act as a “cowardly war crime.”

“Shahid Baqaei Hospital, a children's cancer treatment centre in Ahvaz, was evacuated last night after the US attacked a nearby location,” Esmaeil Baqaei wrote on his X page.
​
“This barbaric attack, reminiscent of Israel’s atrocities against healthcare facilities, caused severe suffering and anxiety upon the hospitalized children and forced the emergency evacuation of 211 patients undergoing chemotherapy.”
​
“This constitutes a cowardly war crime against the most innocent of human beings — children who are bravely fighting for their lives,” he added.
​
“Those who ceaselessly preach human rights, yet deliberately turn a blind eye to the targeting of hospitals and health centers, have forfeited every shred of moral credibility.”
​

📌 Mempools: Where Transactions Wait Before the Block

Main Points
⏺ A mempool is the waiting room for unconfirmed transactions
⏺ Bots, validators, and network actors can see pending activity there
⏺ This post explains why mempools matter for fees, speed, and MEV

1️⃣ What It Is — after you send a transaction, it usually waits before being included in a block.
2️⃣ Why Gas Matters — higher fees increase the chance your transaction gets picked faster.
3️⃣ Where Risk Lives — public mempools let bots see your trade before it executes and try to profit from it.
4️⃣ User Impact — delays, speeding up transactions, cancellations, sandwich attacks, and sudden fee spikes.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — check fees, avoid excessive slippage, and use protected routes for large swaps.
Final Thoughts

A mempool is the blockchain waiting room. But in that room, your transaction is visible not only to validators — also to actors trying to profit from its order.
